metadata.title: TIMSS Third International Mathematics and Science Study Documentation of National Adaptations of International Background Questionnaire Items Populations 1 and 2 Supplement 3 Primary and Middle School Years – 1995 Assessment User Guide for the TIMSS International Database

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is a TIMSS Database User Guide supplement describing how national adaptations of background questionnaire items are coded for secondary analysis. It does not provide an analytic sample, estimation model, or any instructions for applying student or replicate weights to produce achievement estimates. For users working with TIMSS contextual variables, the key “data preparation” step is to select the correct international variable versions and to apply the documented country-specific inclusion/exclusion rules (Code D included; Code X not included) rather than to perform statistical weighting described here. Because this supplement focuses on questionnaire item comparability and database coding, it does not specify weight variables (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or replicate-weight methods; analysts should consult the main TIMSS User Guide for the complex survey design and weighting variables used in the international database.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This supplement is not an empirical study predicting or estimating outcomes from TIMSS student achievement scores; it is documentation for secondary users about which background questionnaire items are available and how national adaptations are coded. Therefore, plausible values (PV-based achievement scores) are not part of the task, and the document does not describe any PV-based missing-data handling strategy. Missing data handling is also not reported because the supplement’s purpose is to flag unavailable or non-comparable questionnaire items (Code X) rather than to impute or delete missing responses in an analysis.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: This supplement does not define an analytic student sample. Instead, it documents country-specific availability and comparability of TIMSS background questionnaire items for secondary analysis. Users should filter the international database variables according to the documented item-level codes: Code D indicates the national data are included in the international variable (with notes on differences), while Code X indicates the national data are not included (e.g., not administered, not applicable, deleted, or not internationally comparable). For Population 2, users must also apply the questionnaire specialization logic (SQ2 vs SQ2(s)) so that students are only assigned variables corresponding to the version administered in their country; variables not administered for a country are coded as 'not administered'.

data.outcome_summary: This document is a TIMSS (Third International Mathematics and Science Study) Database User Guide supplement that explains how national adaptations of background questionnaire items are represented in the international database for secondary analyses. It covers Population 1 and Population 2 questionnaire types for students, teachers, and schools, and provides item-level documentation by country, including the questionnaire item location reference and an abbreviated question description. The core “coding” mechanism is Code D (national data included in the international variable, with notes on differences) versus Code X (national data not included due to non-administration, non-applicability, deletion, or lack of international comparability). For Population 2, it also documents the specialized versus non-specialized student questionnaire versions and the resulting variable availability by country. Because it is documentation rather than an empirical analysis, it does not report model performance metrics, PV handling, or missing-data imputation strategies.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a database documentation supplement rather than an empirical research paper. As such, it does not estimate relationships between predictors and outcomes, does not train or evaluate machine learning models, and does not provide an analytic sample size or per-country student counts. The absence of PV handling and missing-data handling details is by design: the supplement focuses on item comparability coding (Code D vs Code X) and questionnaire-version availability, not on statistical estimation procedures.
